translations.text: Paul and Timothy, servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, together with the bishops and deacons:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I give thanks to God at every remembrance of you;
always, in all my prayers for all of you, I make prayer with joy
because of your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now,
and likewise because of the hope that he who began a good work among you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.

As it is right for me to think this about all of you, because I remember you in my heart, in my bonds and in the defense and confirmation of the gospel, so that all of you may be sharers with me in that grace.
For God is my witness how I long for all of you with the mercy of Christ Jesus;
and this too I pray, that your love may overflow more and more with knowledge and all discernment,
so that you may test what is better, so that you may be true and without stumbling until the day of Christ Jesus,
filled with the fruit of righteousness through Jesus Christ, for the glory and praise of God. 2
I want you to know, brothers, that what has happened to me has come about rather for the advancement of the gospel,
so that these bonds of mine have become manifest in Christ throughout the whole palace and to all others,
and to most of the brothers in the Lord, who trust in my bonds, I dare [?] all the more to speak the word of God without fear.
Some preach Christ out of envy and strife, but some also out of goodwill;
those who proclaim Christ out of strife do so impurely, thinking to bring afflictions upon these bonds of mine,
but others out of love, knowing that I stand for the defense of the gospel.
What then? In every way, whether by pretext or in truth, Christ is preached, and for this I rejoice and will go on rejoicing.
For I know that this will turn out for my salvation through your supplication and the help of the Spirit of Christ Jesus,
according to my expectation and my hope that I will be put to shame in nothing, but that with all boldness, as always, so now too, Christ will be glorified in my body, whether by life or by death.
For to me life is Christ, and death is gain.
But life in this flesh, this is for me the fruit of work, and which I shall choose I do not know.
But I am held between these two: my heart tells me to depart and to be with Christ, which is far more and better.
But remaining in the flesh is more necessary [?] for your sake.
And this I know with hope: that I will remain and attend on all of you for your progress and for the joy of the faith,
so that your boasting may abound in Christ Jesus because of me, through my coming to you again.

Only walk in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ, so that whether I come and see you or am far away, I may hear of you that you stand in one spirit and one mind, striving together for the faith of the gospel,
and that you are in no way frightened by those who attack you, which is for them a sign of destruction, but for you of salvation; and this is from God.
For it has been granted to you for Christ's sake not only to believe in him but also to suffer for him.
Have the same struggle that you saw in me and now hear about from me.
So if there is any consolation from Christ, any comfort of love, any fellowship of the Spirit, any mercy and compassion,
fill up my joy, so that you think the same thing and have the same love; be of one soul and one mind,
doing nothing through attack or vainglory, but in humility each of you regard one another as greater than himself.
Let each of you seek not only his own things, but each of you also those of his neighbor.
Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus,
who, being the image of God, did not count that being equal with God as something to be seized,
but humbled himself and took the image of a servant and became like human beings, and was found in form as a man;
he humbled himself and became obedient even unto death, and that the death of the cross.
Therefore God also exalted him all the more and granted him a name surpassing and greater than all names,
so that at the name of Jesus Christ every knee should bend, of those in heaven and on earth and under the earth,
and every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always been obedient, not only in my coming but now even more in this my being far away, work with fear and trembling for your salvation.
For it is God who works in you both the will and the help for the sake of virtue.
Do all things without murmuring and disputing thoughts,
so that you may be blameless and innocent, children of God, undefiled among a crooked and perverse generation, among whom you appear like luminaries in the world.
Hold the word of life as a boast for me on the day of Christ, that I did not run in vain nor labor in vain.
Even if I am offered upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice and rejoice with you all.
In the same way you also rejoice, and rejoice with me.
And I hope in Christ Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I too may be glad at heart when I learn about you.
For I have no one else so faithful, who would care for you from the heart.
For all seek what is their own, and not what is Christ Jesus's.
But you know his proven character, that as a son serves a father, so he served the gospel with me.
Him, therefore, I hope to send, when I have settled what concerns me, from that point on.
And I trust in the Lord that I too will come soon.
I considered it better to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother and helper and fellow-combatant, and your apostle and minister to my needs,
since he was longing to see all of you and was troubled, because you had heard that he had fallen ill.
And indeed he fell ill, even to the point of death; but God had mercy on him, and not only on him but on me as well, so that grief might not be added to my grief.
Therefore I have sent him speedily, so that you may see him and rejoice again, and I may be free of sorrow.
Receive him in the Lord with all joy, and hold such people in honor,
for because of the work of Christ he came near to death, offering up his life, so that he might complete the service to me that you lacked.
From now on, brothers, rejoice in the Lord! To write the same things to you is not irksome to me, and for you it is a safeguard.
Beware of the dogs, beware of the evil workers, look out for the mutilation,
for we are the circumcision, who serve by the Spirit of God and boast in Christ Jesus and do not trust in the flesh,
although I too have hope even in the flesh. If anyone else thinks to have hope in the flesh, I have more:
circumcised on the eighth day, of the race of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews, as to the law a Pharisee,
in zeal I persecuted the churches, and in the righteousness of the law I was blameless.
But whatever was gain to me, this I have counted as loss for the sake of Christ.

Indeed, I also count everything as loss because of the surpassing knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, for whose sake I have suffered the loss of everything and have counted it as refuse, so that I may gain Christ
and be found in him, not having my own righteousness from the law, but through faith in Christ, the righteousness from God by faith,
to know him and the power of his resurrection and the sharing of his sufferings, being made conformed to his death,
so that somehow I may attain to the resurrection of the dead.
Not that I have already received it, or have already been made perfect; but I press on so that I may lay hold of that for which I too was laid hold of by Christ Jesus.
Brothers, I no longer consider myself to have laid hold of it; but this one thing I do: I forget what is behind and reach out to what is ahead,
and with care I pursue the crown of the heavenly calling of God in Christ Jesus.
As many of us, then, as are perfect, let us think this; and if you think anything else, may God reveal that also to you.
But to whatever point we have reached, let us think the same thing and stand by the same rule.
Become imitators of me, brothers, and watch those who walk in this way, just as we are an example for you.
For many walk about of whom I have often told you, and now I tell you with weeping, about those enemies of the cross of Christ,
whose end is destruction, whose god is the belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who think about earthly things.
But our citizenship is in heaven, from where we await the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ,
who will transform these bodies of our lowliness, so that they may be conformed to the body of his glory, according to the working of his power, and to subject all things to himself.
Therefore, my beloved and longed-for brothers, my joys and my crowns, stand firm in this way in the Lord, beloved.
I entreat Euodia and I entreat Syntyche to think the same thing in the Lord;

yes, I entreat you too, faithful yokefellow, help these women, who struggled together with me in the gospel, along with Clement and the rest of my fellow workers, whose names are written in the book of life.
Rejoice always in the Lord; again I say: rejoice.
Let your humility be made known to all people. The Lord is near.
Do not worry about anything, but by every prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God,
and may the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, guard your hearts and your minds through Christ Jesus.

From now on, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is honourable, whatever is just, whatever is holy, whatever is lovely, whatever is praiseworthy, whatever is virtuous, and whatever is commended, think about these things.
What you learned and received and heard and saw in me, do that; and may the God of peace be with you.
I rejoiced greatly in the Lord that now at last you have blossomed again in your concern for me. You were indeed concerned, but you were held back.
I do not say this to you because of any need, for I have learned to be content in whatever state I am in.
I know how to be brought low, and I know how to have plenty; in all things and in every circumstance I have been trained: to be full and to be hungry, to have plenty and to be in want.
I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
Yet you did well to share in these afflictions of mine.

And you yourselves also know, Philippians, that at the beginning of the gospel, when I set out from Macedonia, not a single church shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving except you alone.
For even in Thessalonica you sent help for my needs once and again.
It is not that I seek the gift; rather, I seek the fruit that increases to your credit.
I have everything and I have more than enough. I am filled, having received from Epaphroditus what you sent: a fragrant aroma, an offered sacrifice pleasing to God.
And may my God fill your every need according to his riches in glory through Christ Jesus.
And to our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen.
Greet all the saints in Christ Jesus. The brothers who are with me greet you.
All the saints greet you, and especially those of the household of Caesar.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
